texts: In Marfan syndrome, a ratio of maximal aortic root cross-sectional area (cm²) to height (m) above 10 is an indication for prophylactic root replacement; a ratio of 12 means operate.
The ratio corrects for body size and predicts dissection better than the diameter alone in tall Marfan patients.
A root that grows from one yearly scan to the next adds to the case.
Beta-blockers and angiotensin receptor blockers slow growth but do not replace surgery once the threshold is passed.
Waiting six months for another CT risks a dissection.
In the picture, the cat's slice outweighs the height chart on the scale, and Franky replaces the swollen salsa bowls with a white root.
Memory hook: when the slice outweighs the height, change the root.
